lattice_constant.note: value at x = 0; the 13C term changes a by at most 0.000 53 Å (pure 13C), below the 3.567 Å shown. Cross-checks: COD 9011575 gives 3.56679 Å at 291.15 K and COD 2300702 gives 3.566636(7) Å at 293 K, all within 0.0006 Å.

structure.value: diamond cubic, space group Fd-3m (No. 227); two interpenetrating face-centred cubic lattices offset by a/4 (1,1,1); 8 atoms per conventional cubic cell
structure.source: Crystallography Open Database entry 2300702 (Houben et al., J. Appl. Cryst. 56, 633 (2023), doi:10.1107/S1600576723002819): _space_group_name_H-M_alt 'F d -3 m :2', _cell_formula_units_Z 8, C1 at 8a

cc_bond_length.note: formula: d = sqrt(3) a / 4 (nearest-neighbour distance); inputs: diamond.lattice_constant; COD 2300702 lists C1-C1 1.5444 Å for its 3.566636 Å cell; same formula

bond_angle.note: formula: theta = arccos(-1/3) (tetrahedral); inputs: diamond.structure; COD 2300702 lists 109.471°

geometry.value: a substitutional nitrogen adjacent to a lattice vacancy; the NV symmetry axis lies along one of the four <111> crystallographic directions
geometry.source: Barry et al., 'Sensitivity optimization for NV-diamond magnetometry', Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004 (2020), arXiv 1903.08176v2, Sec. I.A, p. 2 and Fig. 1a ('a substitutional nitrogen fixed adjacent to a vacancy within the rigid carbon lattice')

n_v_distance.note: formula: N-V distance = C-C bond length (ideal, unrelaxed lattice sites); inputs: diamond.cc_bond_length, nv.geometry; relaxation of the atoms around the vacancy is not modelled, so it is not drawn

D.source: Barry et al., 'Sensitivity optimization for NV-diamond magnetometry', Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004 (2020), arXiv 1903.08176v2, Sec. I.C, p. 4 ('D ≈ 2.87 GHz')

gamma.source: Barry et al., 'Sensitivity optimization for NV-diamond magnetometry', Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004 (2020), arXiv 1903.08176v2, Eq. (6), gamma = g_e mu_B / h
gamma.note: Barry et al. give g_e ≈ 2.003, i.e. gamma ≈ 28.03 MHz/mT; 28.025 MHz/mT is the brief's value (free-electron g = 2.0023, also used by ODMR-Lab). The two differ by 0.03 %.

g_factor_barry.source: Barry et al., 'Sensitivity optimization for NV-diamond magnetometry', Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004 (2020), arXiv 1903.08176v2, Sec. I.C, Eq. (2), p. 4 ('g_e ≈ 2.003 is the NV electronic g-factor')

gamma_from_barry_g.note: formula: gamma = g_NV mu_B / h; inputs: nv.g_factor_barry, electron.bohr_magneton_over_h; Barry's g ≈ 2.003 gives 28.03 MHz/mT; physics.json uses 28.025 MHz/mT, the free-electron value (CODATA 2022 gamma_e/2pi = 28.02495 MHz/mT)

gamma_vs_codata_relative.note: formula: (gamma_physics - gamma_e/2pi) / (gamma_e/2pi); inputs: nv.gamma, electron.gyromagnetic_ratio_over_2pi_per_mT; physics.json's 28.025 MHz/mT is the CODATA free-electron value rounded to 5 digits; its TO_CONFIRM status is inherited

gslac_field.note: formula: B = D / gamma (m_s = -1 meets m_s = 0, field along the axis); inputs: nv.D, nv.gamma; the scene's field control stops at 5 mT, far below this crossing

levels.value: nu± = D ± (g_e mu_B / h) B_z: m_s = 0 at 0, m_s = ±1 at D ± gamma B for a field along the NV axis
levels.source: Barry et al., 'Sensitivity optimization for NV-diamond magnetometry', Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004 (2020), arXiv 1903.08176v2, Sec. I.C, Eqs. (5)-(6), p. 5

ramsey.value: Ramsey on the {|0>, |+1>} pair: pi/2 pulse, free precession for tau, pi/2 pulse; phase phi = gamma_e B tau with gamma_e = g_e mu_B / hbar, i.e. phi = 2 pi gamma B tau with gamma in Hz/T
ramsey.source: Barry et al., 'Sensitivity optimization for NV-diamond magnetometry', Rev. Mod. Phys. 92, 015004 (2020), arXiv 1903.08176v2, Sec. I.D, pp. 5-6, and Sec. I.E, p. 6

spin_operators.source: standard spin-1 matrices, as used for the NV Hamiltonian H = D S_z^2 + gamma B.S in data/math_checks.json (Barry et al. Eq. 2)

superposition_spin_tilt.note: formula: <S> of (|0> + e^{i phi}|+1>)/sqrt2 is (cos phi/sqrt2, sin phi/sqrt2, 1/2); tilt = arccos(<S_z>/|<S>|); inputs: nv.spin_operators, nv.ramsey; = arccos(1/sqrt3); expectation values checked symbolically in Wolfram Language

superposition_spin_length.note: formula: |<S>| = sqrt(1/2 + 1/4) (units of hbar); inputs: nv.spin_operators, nv.ramsey

dark_state.note: formula: sigma+ light drives m_F -> m_F + 1; 5²P1/2 has F' = 1, 2 only, so from m_F = +2 there is no m_F' = +3 to reach: the stretched state is dark to sigma+ D1 light; inputs: rb87.nuclear_spin, rb87.p12_hfs_splitting, rb87.dark_state_table; levels from Steck Fig. 3; QuSpin: at zero field the atoms 'become largely transparent'

vdw_radius.source: Mantina, Chamberlin, Valero, Cramer & Truhlar, 'Consistent van der Waals radii for the whole main group', J. Phys. Chem. A 113, 5806-5812 (2009), doi:10.1021/jp8111556, abstract: 'The newly determined radii (in Å) are ... Rb, 3.03'
vdw_radius.note: van der Waals radius on Bondi's scale; drawn as the atom's size. A free atom has no sharp edge.

bloch_equation.source: Sulai et al., 'Characterizing atomic magnetic gradiometers for fetal magnetocardiography', arXiv 1906.03227 (2019), Appendix B, Eq. (B1), p. 10: R optical pumping rate, s photon spin vector, Omega = gamma B, Gamma total spin relaxation rate

steady_state.value: = R / (Gamma'(Gamma'^2 + Omega^2)) [Gamma' Omega_y + Omega_z Omega_x, -Gamma' Omega_x + Omega_y Omega_z, Gamma'^2 + Omega_z^2], Gamma' = Gamma + R
steady_state.source: Sulai et al., 'Characterizing atomic magnetic gradiometers for fetal magnetocardiography', arXiv 1906.03227 (2019), Appendix B, Eq. (B2), p. 10
steady_state.note: arXiv v1 prints -Gamma'^2 in the z component; +Gamma'^2 is the sign that solves Eq. (B1) (Lean theorem opm_steady_state; Wolfram check below)

dimensionless_form.value: with s = z, w = Omega/Gamma' and P in units of R/Gamma': dP/dtau = z - P + w x P; steady state P* = (z + w x z + (w.z) w) / (1 + |w|^2)
dimensionless_form.source: Sulai et al., 'Characterizing atomic magnetic gradiometers for fetal magnetocardiography', arXiv 1906.03227 (2019), Eqs. (B1)-(B2), rescaled
dimensionless_form.note:
tau is dimensionless time. The left side of (B1) is 2 d/dt and the paper does not give how follows

, so tau is not converted to seconds; the steady state does not depend on it.

cell_temperature.source: Sulai et al., 'Characterizing atomic magnetic gradiometers for fetal magnetocardiography', arXiv 1906.03227 (2019), Sec. III, p. 2 ('We heat the cells up to a temperature of 150 °C')
cell_temperature.note: QuSpin states the QZFM cell 'runs at ~150 °C' (QuSpin technology page, 'How the QZFM works', https://quspin.com/technology/ (accessed 2026-11-15))

cell_density.source: Sulai et al., 'Characterizing atomic magnetic gradiometers for fetal magnetocardiography', arXiv 1906.03227 (2019), Sec. III, p. 2 ('the equilibrium density is n = 10^14 cm^-3')
cell_density.note: Sulai's cell holds rubidium (isotope not stated) with about 200 Torr N2 and Ne buffer gas

mean_atom_spacing.note: formula: mean spacing n^(-1/3); inputs: opm_model.cell_density; neighbouring atoms lie this far apart on average: far outside the scene, which shows one atom

pump.value: circularly polarised light resonant with the Rb D1 line at 795 nm polarises the atoms along z
pump.source: Sulai et al., 'Characterizing atomic magnetic gradiometers for fetal magnetocardiography', arXiv 1906.03227 (2019), Sec. III, p. 2
pump.note: QuSpin does not state the QZFM's laser line; the QZFM is single-beam ('based on zero-field resonance with a single laser beam', QuSpin technology page, 'How the QZFM works', https://quspin.com/technology/ (accessed 2026-11-15))

structure.source: Crystallography Open Database entry 9011577 (Trucano & Chen, 'Structure of graphite by neutron diffraction', Nature 258, 136 (1975), doi:10.1038/258136a0): _space_group_IT_number 194, atom sites

layer_spacing_d002.note: formula: layer spacing d(002) = c/2; inputs: graphite.c

cc_in_plane.note: formula: in-plane C-C = a / sqrt3; inputs: graphite.a, graphite.structure

d100.note: formula: d(100) = a sqrt3 / 2 (hexagonal d_hk0); inputs: graphite.a; the in-plane fringe spacing often reported in TEM of carbon dots; here it is graphite's value, not a measurement on the patch's dots

patch_dot_lattice_fringe.source: Tabatabaee, Naghdi, Peyravian, Kiani, Golmohammadi, 'An Invisible Dermal Nanotattoo-Based Smart Wearable Sensor for eDiagnostics of Jaundice', ACS Nano 18(41), 28012-28025 (2024), doi:10.1021/acsnano.4c06191 (abstract)
patch_dot_lattice_fringe.note: the abstract gives no TEM lattice fringes or dot size; the full text and SI are paywalled (SI request returned HTTP 403 on 2026-11-15). The scene uses graphite's lattice instead.

patch_dot_size.source: Tabatabaee, Naghdi, Peyravian, Kiani, Golmohammadi, 'An Invisible Dermal Nanotattoo-Based Smart Wearable Sensor for eDiagnostics of Jaundice', ACS Nano 18(41), 28012-28025 (2024), doi:10.1021/acsnano.4c06191 (abstract)
patch_dot_size.note: not in the abstract; the drawn fragment's extent is a display choice

mechanism.value: selective recovery of quenched fluorescence of the carbon-quantum-dot tattoo upon the blue light used for jaundice phototherapy, used for bilirubin sensing
mechanism.source: Tabatabaee, Naghdi, Peyravian, Kiani, Golmohammadi, 'An Invisible Dermal Nanotattoo-Based Smart Wearable Sensor for eDiagnostics of Jaundice', ACS Nano 18(41), 28012-28025 (2024), doi:10.1021/acsnano.4c06191, abstract

quenching_model.source: physics.json cqd_quenching: quenching/recovery model and constants from doi:10.1021/acsnano.4c06191
quenching_model.note: not public, so quenching and recovery are shown only as on/off states

physics_label.value: carbon dots are fluorescent nanoparticles; their emission is not a spin-based quantum measurement
physics_label.source: Tabatabaee, Naghdi, Peyravian, Kiani, Golmohammadi, 'An Invisible Dermal Nanotattoo-Based Smart Wearable Sensor for eDiagnostics of Jaundice', ACS Nano 18(41):28012-28025 (2024), doi:10.1021/acsnano.4c06191, PubMed 39356285 (abstract)
physics_label.note: general physics label, not a claim of the paper

emission_wavelength.source: Mendeley Data doi:10.17632/cmfbrvrb8y.1, external measurement records (general carbon dots, not the patch)

emission_colour.source: CIE 1931 2° standard observer colour-matching table (via colour-science 0.4.7, colour.MSDS_CMFS['CIE 1931 2 Degree Standard Observer']); sRGB per IEC 61966-2-1 (D65)
emission_colour.note: formula: CIE 1931 colour-matching table -> XYZ -> linear sRGB, negatives clipped, scaled to full brightness, sRGB gamma; inputs: Measured carbon-dot emission maximum (most common value) wavelength

carbon_sp3.note: checked against the package's transcription, not the paywalled article

checks.tool: Wolfram Language (WolframLanguageEvaluator via the Wolfram MCP connector), run 2026-11-15

bloch_steady_state.what: |z - P* + w x P*| for 2000 random w in [-5, 5]^3

nv_splitting.what: |(nu+ - nu-) - 2 gamma B| and |(nu+ + nu-)/2 - D| for B = 0 to 5 mT in 0.01 mT steps

note: Values with tag calculated carry their formula and inputs. Display choices made by the scenes (slow-down factors, magnified level spacings, sphere-size fractions, arrow lengths) are not constants and are stated in each scene's info panel.
